intent: The undeploy confirmation's consequence takes the consequence role, and its buttons stop being unreachable on a narrow screen.
rationale: DT-0016's ruling, one page over, and for the same reason: this consequence says the agent stops scanning a market it may hold a position in, and it currently wears the anonymous border DT-0004 retired. Undeploy is the sibling of deploy in every other respect — same shell, same shared buttons, same confirmation binding — so the two disagreeing about how a consequence looks is drift rather than a decision. The reversibility this page's copy states ('the agent stays configured and can be redeployed') is carried by the words; it is not a reason to lighten the block, because what the block announces is that scanning stops now.

design.layout: Unchanged in order; the action row stacks under the tablet breakpoint and sits inline above it.

default.content: consequence: the block takes the consequence role — color.consequence.subtle background, 1px color.consequence.border border, radius.2, space.4 padding, color.text.primary; role=alert stays and the sentence stays verbatim. perform-undeploy: column at space.3 gap, wrapped row at breakpoint.tablet, both controls full width below it and auto above — the archive page's treatment.

responsive.mobile: Buttons stacked, each full width, each at the size.control.min floor.

acceptance: The consequence block renders on color.consequence.subtle with a 1px color.consequence.border border at radius.2, and keeps role=alert
At a 320px viewport the submit and cancel are stacked, each full width, each at least size.control.min tall
At tablet width and above the two controls sit inline as they do today
The submit remains accent-styled, never danger
Zero copy changes anywhere on the page
No raw color, spacing, or size literal is introduced

references.value: Backlog 166. DT-0016's ruling applied to the sibling page; decides nothing new.
